root_cause.text: The EFI memory map provided by firmware incorrectly reports a portion of the hypervisor-owned Gunyah metadata region (0x91a88000–0x91afffff) as conventional memory instead of reserved, causing the kernel to allocate from and access hypervisor memory, leading to synchronous external aborts.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message explicitly state: "the EFI memory map provided by firmware only reserves the subrange 0x91a40000–0x91a87fff (288 KiB). The remaining portion (0x91a88000–0x91afffff) is incorrectly reported as conventional memory... As a result, the allocator may hand out PFNs inside the hypervisor owned region, causing fatal aborts when the kernel accesses those addresses." The patch adds a reserved-memory carveout with `no-map` for the full region at 0x91a80000 (size 0x80000) to prevent this.
